name: Strontium iridate
equilibrium_context: Jeff=1/2 spin-orbit-coupled insulator, antiferromagnetic below about 240 K; structurally and electronically analogous to La2CuO4
summary: Included in the register explicitly as a corrective case: the work refutes the widespread classification as a Mott insulator.

driven_states.emergent_property: Optical excitation closes the gap; in time-resolved ARPES, weakly renormalized electronic bands appear in the former gap region.
further_sources: Dean et al., Nature Materials 15, 601 (2016), doi:10.1038/nmat4641
driven_states.caveat: The most important negative finding of the register. Comparing the light-induced gap closing with the expected temperature and doping evolution of Mott gaps yields, according to the authors, clear evidence that the insulating state does NOT originate from Mott correlations. A correlated band insulator is proposed whose gap is sustained by antiferromagnetic correlations. Sr2IrO4 should therefore not be listed as a photoinduced Mott transition.

gaps: Photon energy and fluence not verified against the full text.
